findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed member of staff to not use barrier when turning off handwashing faucet. Discussed with PIC, education on proper handwashing was provided and employee rewashed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed container of cut potatoes to be resting on floor. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and potatoes were moved to table. Ensure all food items are kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed multiple sets of plates to not be inverted or stored under shelf. Discussed with PIC, plates were moved to under shelf unit. Ensure clean plates are stored in way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Observed the triple sink to the right of dish machine to be leaking at the faucet. Discussed with PIC, leak will be serviced by a licensed plumber. Ensure no leaks are present within facility.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed a container of sauce to be hot holding at 120F. Discussed with PIC, the hot holding unit was not plugged in. The sauce was moved to the stove and reheated to 165F. Ensure any TCS food being hot held is kept at or above 135F. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed caulking to be missing/damaged in the following areas:
1) To the left of the kitchen dish machine.
2) The triple sink to the right of the dish machine.

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being checked regularly. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
In-house made cocktail sauce was observed to be held past the 7 day maximum.  Discussed with PIC, who discarded items.  Ensure foods are discarded after 7 days.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following physical facility areas in need of repairs:
1. Majority of the equipment in the kitchen needs re-caulked to the wall. The kitchen was recently re-painted and the equipment was not re-caulked at this time (was expected to be).
2. The facility had a fire recently. The wall with the AC unit (to the right of the cook line) was replaced with new stainless steel and Nudo board. The wood that is covering the window (where AC unit is) needs to be painted and the framing should be caulked.
3. The wall above the hot holding steam table (to the left of the cook line) needs re-dry walled and painted.
4. Coving is needed near the mop area and by the salad prep cooler.
5. Bar hand sink is missing caulk to the wall - caulk the hand sink.

Discussed the above areas with PIC. Ensure repairs before the next routine inspection.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine to only being sanitizing at 10 ppm. PIC adjusted the sanitizer line and Inspector re-tested the dish machine for bleach after a cycle - 50 ppm. The dish machine was then run a 3rd time without adjusting the sanitizer line - 10 ppm again. The line needs to be corrected so it sanitizes on its own at 50-200 ppm of bleach. MJ Kellner was called to service the machine. Facility has test strips to verify sanitizer concentrations. Do not use the dish machine until it is repaired by MJ Kellner. The wash, rinse, sanitize process should be done in the 3 compartment sink or wash and rinse within the dish machine, sanitize in the 3 compartment sink basin. Discussed with PIC and the dish washer. Ensure staff is aware not to utilize the dish machine until repaired. Inspector will follow-up on 10/2/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the interior of the basement ice machine to have a layer of mold on the ceiling. Inspector showed PIC with a flashlight. Inspector instructed PIC to remove all the ice and wash, rinse, sanitize the inside of the ice machine. PIC had an employee do this process during the inspection. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean out the ice machine to prevent mold build-up. Discussed with PIC. COS.

Observed the walk-in cooler shelving to have mold on the grates. Shelving is made of plastic and can be snapped off. PIC had staff begin to take the shelving a part and bring upstairs (walk-in cooler is in basement) to wash, rinse, and sanitize. Discussed routine cleaning of cooler shelves with PIC. Ensure staff routinely cleans the shelving units to prevent debris and mold build-up. Inspector will follow-up on 10/6/23.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the large two door reach-in cooler within the kitchen to have the gasket/seal coming away from both the doors. Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure gasket is replaced or repaired before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Walk-in cooler fan has a layer of dust.
2. Dish machine sprayer has a layer of food debris and grime on the squeezer handle and top of the sprayer.
3. The fan in the dish machine area has a layer of dust.

Discussed routine cleaning of non food-contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure the above areas are cleaned before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed the following physical facility areas in need of repairs:
1. Majority of the equipment in the kitchen needs re-caulked to the wall. The kitchen was recently re-painted and the equipment was not re-caulked at this time (was expected to be).
2. The facility had a fire last week. The wall with the AC unit (to the right of the cook line) was replaced with new stainless steel and Nudo board. The wood that is covering the window (where AC unit is) needs to be painted and the framing should be caulked.
3. The wall above the hot holding steam table (to the left of the cook line) needs re-dry walled and painted.
4. Paint the bare wood at the dish machine sprayer and the potato ricer (both are mounted to the wall with wooden planks). 
5. Coving is needed near the mop area and by the salad prep cooler.
6. There are two holes in the wall and trim missing by the mop sink/large two door reach-in cooler.
7. Bar hand sink is missing caulk to the wall - caulk the hand sink.
8. The men’s bathroom has base coving coming away, as well as an area where a soap dispenser once was (wall should be made smooth and easily cleanable - fill the holes with caulking). 

Discussed the above areas with PIC. Ensure repairs before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed no allergen training certifications for the certified food protection manager’s (CFPM’s). Facility has 4-5 CFPM’s and all need to complete the allergen training certification online. Print copies of the certification for the public health binder. Certification is valid for 3 years. Correct by the next routine inspection. Provided educational handout on where to complete certification online. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/7/23.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple coolers to lack thermometers. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all cold holding units have a thermometer within unit. Purchase extra thermometers to have on hand in case of being lost or broken. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed no allergen training certifications for the certified food protection manager’s. Discussed with PIC. Provided educational handout on how to re-take the certification. Valid for 3 years. Only the CFPM’s should complete. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the dish machine was registering below 50 ppm CL on inspector test strips (approximately 10). The bottle of sanitizer is observed to need replacing. The bottle was replaced and the machine primed. After the machine was observed with 50 ppm CL in a normal wash cycle.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Dried potato pieces/ debris is observed on the fry slicer. PIC believes that it is likely was not cleaned at closing Sunday. Food contact surfaces should be cleaned regularly (within 4 hours) when in use and at the end of the night. The slicer was taken apart and ran through dish during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

The chest freezer used for vegetables (located in the basement) has what appears to be corn and beans spilled in the bottom. An accumulation of frost indicates that it has been there for a significant period of time. PIC instructed to clean non-food contact items as needed to ensure clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Multiple locations observed in need of cleaning: 1) the window frame around the AC window unit in the kitchen. A container of spoons is observed on top of the unit and the surrounding area needs to be maintained clean. Area cleaned during the inspection. 2) The lip of the shelf above the prep counter across from the grills/ fryers. Food debris observed. Area cleaned during the inspection. 3) The shelf and floor where raw onions are stored in the basement. Onion debris observed. Area needs to be maintained clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. They then proceeded to manipulate the paper towel dispenser with a bare hand for the drying implement. Education has taken place.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the dish machine in the kitchen is not properly sanitizing dishes. Priming the machine brought the concentration up to correct levels. PIC stated that they would contact MJ Kelner for a service call to ensure the machine functions correctly in the future.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Two containers of knives are observed stored in containers with crumbs in the bottom of the containers. Containers and knives were sent to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf). The Dish machine in the bar area is observed with a sanitizer concentration of approximately 0-10 ppm CL. Label indicates a minimum of 50 ppm CL to adequately sanitize food contact surfaces. Glasses will be moved to the kitchen dish machine for sanitizing until service can be performed by MJ Kelner on the machine.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). Milk is observed in the bar cooler to not have a date mark placed on it when opened. The container also has a use by date of 3/17/21 (yesterday) and is approximately half empty. A discussion took place with the PIC and they are aware that milk is a TCS food requiring date marking when opened. The milk was discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11 (Pf) The Person in Charge shall ensure that: (O)  “Food Employees and Conditional Employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as relate to disease that are transmissible through food as specified under 2-201.11 (A). On arrival, reporting agreements were not available for the inspector to see. Copies were given and filled out during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11  (P) All foods intended for consumption must be in safe and unadulterated condition. Ice in both the bar ice bin and the fountain drink machine is observed with black and brown spots. Both locations come from the same ice machine downstairs. The ice machine does not appear to have any accumulated contaminants at this time, but was serviced this morning. The ice was discarded and fresh ice received that was free of contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Wash, rinse, sanitize food contact surfaces so that they remain free of soilage. The potato slicer in the kitchen is observed with dried on food debris. The item was taken apart and cleaned/ sanitized to correct.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Foods should be cooled to 41°F or less within 6 hours. Cheese sauce in the walk in cooler was observed with a date mark for 2/26 (yesterday) and was probed out of temperature. The internal temperature near the edge of the container was 44°F and the internal temperature near the center of the container was 47°F. Cheese sauce was discarded during the inspection. Inspector suggested either using smaller pans or using ice wands to facilitate rapid cooling.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 (A)(B) (P) Bleach sanitizer bucket in the kitchen area bleached out the inspector's test strips, indicating that it is to strong. PIC is instructed to make solutions per the instructions on the label which indicate 200 ppm concentration. The bucket was remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11  (C) 1) The caulking behind the hand sink in the kitchen is severely cracked. 2) The caulking around the men's bathroom hand sinks is severely cracked. PIC is instructed to maintain these items smooth and easily clean able.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 (A) (P) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code.

Probes used for roasts were observed stored in water. Discussion with the PIC revealed that they are placed in the water to cool them off after use in an oven and left overnight. Inspector discussed with the PIC that food contact items should be cleaned and sanitized after use. The items were cleaned during the inspection.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 (C) (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The roof of the ice machine was observed with black mold during the inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to clean the machine early enough so as to prevent the accumulation of organisms in the machine.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 (C) (C) Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The microwave in the kitchen was observed with the roof door and tray soiled with food residues. The item was brought the attention of the PIC and it was cleaned during the inspection.
